title: Happy Number
pattern: Cycle detection with slow and fast pointers
statement: Replace a number by the **sum of the squares of its digits**, and repeat. A number is *happy* if this process reaches `1`. Otherwise it loops forever without ever reaching 1. Return `True` if `n` is happy.
idea: Each number leads to exactly one next number, like a linked list. The chain either arrives at 1 (and then stays there, since 1² = 1) or runs into a **cycle**.
A cycle can be detected without remembering every number seen: let `slow` advance one step at a time and `fast` two steps. In a cycle, `fast` eventually catches up with `slow`.
So loop until `fast` reaches 1 (happy) or `fast` meets `slow` (a cycle that does not contain 1).

complexity.timeWhy: The numbers shrink very quickly (any number below 1000 maps to at most 243), and the cycle is short.
complexity.spaceWhy: Two numbers — no set of seen values.

steps.text: Our example: **`n = 19`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
